_comment: The iOS build number, and the Android twin of packaging/android/version.json.
WHY THIS FILE EXISTS. It did not, and that cost a submission. The Android
scaffold has always read versionName out of the root package.json and
stamped it into Gradle; the iOS scaffold stamped nothing, so the Xcode
project kept whatever number was last typed into it by hand. That number
was 1.3.1 - the value used as the EXAMPLE in APP-STORE-WALKTHROUGH.md - and
on 9 Sep 2026 a binary carrying the whole 1.5.6 game went to App Store
Connect labelled 1.3.1, because setting the field was a step a human had to
MARKETING_VERSION       from the root package.json (the version players see)
CURRENT_PROJECT_VERSION from build below (the number Apple counts uploads by)
Apple requires the build number to be unique WITHIN a marketing version, and
to go up. Raise build by one for every upload of the same version; when the
version in package.json changes you may start again at 1, but going up is
always safe and never wrong. Record what Apple accepted, and never reuse a
number - a spent build number is spent even if the upload was discarded.
